replies.body:
Thanks for pointing this out, the server-side tools slipped my mind completely.

But I think for the `counts` metric it doesn't make sense treat client-side and server-side differently. It would make sense for the `duration` metrics.

I went with the following wording
>    Client-side tool calls (tools executed by the agent or framework) are
      always counted. Server-side tool calls (tools executed by the model provider)
      should be counted where supported.

Not a strong opinion though, feel free push back, if you believe the "where supported" would introduce too much inconsistency.

Thinking about it, it changes how we count things - e.g. when agent is doing tool call itself, it's counting method calls, if we include server/built-in, it would need to count tool parts in the LLM response too to know that it happened.

I can argue since we don't count sub-agent tool calls for this invocation, we should be consistent and count built-ins under `gen_ai.inferece.tool_call` (in the future if someone is interested in adding it).

I'd be in favor saying we don't count model built-in tools
Or, when you're calling a remote agent, potential future `gen_ai.client.invoke_agent.tool_calls` would include built-ins.

> I'd be in favor saying we don't count model built-in tools

So it would be consistent with the number of execute_tool spans? SGTM.

Another option if we don't want to drop them is to use a well known dummy `gen_ai.agent.name` to represent model/server side tool calls. I do wonder if agent frameworks are generally able to instrument it though.

SG, changed the wording to only include client-side tools

>    Only client-side tool calls (tools executed by the agent or framework)
      are counted. Tools executed server-side by the model provider (for
      example, provider built-in web search or code execution) are not
      counted here.

threads.body:
Sorry, I know I proposed some variation of these names, but now suggesting to bikeshed a bit.

I want to keep operation name inside metric name (e.g. we have `gen_ai.invoke_agent.duration` and new metrics should be consistent with it). 

I've had a consilium with a couple of AI agents to find alternatives and curious what you think.

Surprisingly AIs are saying that `per_invocation` is not cool and that something like this

```
gen_ai.invoke_agent.inference_calls
gen_ai.invoke_agent.tool_calls
```

would be as descriptive. 

If we want to add other things like delegations, they would fit nicely.
If we want to have something similar under `invoke_workflow`, it'd work too - `gen_ai.invoke_workflow.agent_calls`. 

Alternative:

```
gen_ai.invoke_agent.inference_call.count
gen_ai.invoke_agent.tool_call.count
```

(I prefer the first version because it's shorter)

/cc @trask in case he has a preference. We had a lot of discussions in the past on .count suffix but based on my analysis they never covered histograms. The closest to this we have is [`rpc.client|server.requests|responses_per_rpc`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/36a02e612491e8b7bfd92f074b40fce6c0542929/model/rpc/deprecated/metrics-deprecated.yaml#L2) (now deprecated)
